opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
Jesus Walks on Water

You’re reacting the right way—**it is insane** if you think about it honestly. Picture it without softening it: it’s dark, they’re already strained, rowing against wind and current, far from shore, and then they see a figure moving across the water toward them. There is no category for that, no framework, no immediate recognition—just the shock of something that does not belong to the natural order. Their first reaction wasn’t faith; it was fear. They thought it was something unnatural, even threatening, and that matters because it tells you something real about human response. What changes the moment is not the miracle itself, but the voice: *“It is I; do not be afraid.”* Before that, there is only fear; after that, recognition. And if you ask honestly what you would do, your body would tense, your mind would scramble to explain it and fail, and you would feel that sharp edge of fear before anything else. Only after recognition would you move toward Him—and that is exactly what they did when they wanted to take Him into the boat.

Then something even stranger happens: the boat is immediately at the shore to which they were heading. No transition, no long effort, just arrival. Don’t miss the structure of this moment—struggle, fear, then recognition leading to reception and sudden completion. They had been rowing hard, making slow progress, and then the distance collapses once He is received. This is where it meets you directly. You’ve been in that same mode—working, pushing, trying to manage everything—and then there are moments where God feels suddenly close, almost disruptive, not immediately comforting but overwhelming. Most people think they would be calm if they saw Him clearly, but that’s not true; you would be shaken because your sense of reality just broke. The invitation remains the same: *“Do not be afraid.”* You don’t have to understand everything or push harder. The shift happens when you recognize Him, receive Him into what you’re already in, and allow that presence to do what your effort could not—because what felt like distance begins to close far faster than you could have managed on your own.
